headline: Max thrust per nozzle 5000 N: +81.2 kg of designed hardware (1/7 lines met by catalog parts, 2 custom part types, 4 needing sourcing); p_success 77% -> 55% after adding the designed hardware.

requirements.label: Peak thrust per nozzle
requirements.derived_from: max over all 10 nozzles and time steps of throttle x thrust_force_max, witness schedule (traj_5000.json), nominal rollout

requirements.label: Nozzle bracket design load (peak thrust, margin applied; part adds safety factor 2.0 on yield)
requirements.derived_from: peak per-nozzle thrust of the witness schedule (traj_5000.json), nominal rollout

requirements.label: Peak propellant mass flow per nozzle
requirements.derived_from: peak thrust / (Isp x g0) with Isp = 70 s (assumption, unverified); witness schedule (traj_5000.json), nominal rollout

requirements.label: Total impulse of the maneuver
requirements.derived_from: sum over nozzles and time of force x dt, witness schedule (traj_5000.json), nominal rollout

requirements.label: Propellant mass for the maneuver
requirements.derived_from: total impulse / (Isp x g0), Isp = 70 s (assumption, unverified); witness schedule (traj_5000.json), nominal rollout

requirements.label: Tank water volume at 300 bar fill (usable down to 10 bar)
requirements.derived_from: N2 stored isothermally 300->10 bar at 20 C: max(ideal gas 71.18 L, van der Waals 80.18 L) for the propellant above; van der Waals N2 constants a=1.370 L^2*bar/mol^2, b=0.0387 L/mol (textbook, not verified against a cited page); ideal-gas value also computed, the larger required tank volume is used. Storage pressure and minimum supply pressure are defaults

requirements.label: Tank working pressure
requirements.derived_from: design default (a rated 300 bar Type-4 cylinder class); not derived from the simulation

requirements.label: Peak landing contact load (x vehicle weight)
requirements.derived_from: peak contact normal force in the 0.3 s after first touchdown (517961 N, MuJoCo contact solver) / (vehicle mass 1300 kg x g); witness schedule (traj_5000.json), nominal rollout. CAVEAT: the model is a rigid body with no suspension compliance, so this contact load depends on the solver's contact stiffness and is a crude upper-end figure, not a validated landing load

check.label: simplified model, needs FEA

extra_checks.method: bolt-hole bearing on the plate, hand calc: F / (n d t) vs yield/SF
extra_checks.label: simplified model, needs FEA

custom_parts.note: Gussets, bolt preload, fatigue and the nozzle's own mounting flange are not modelled.

custom_parts.name: Tank cradle saddle (2 per tank)

check.method: saddle plate as a simply supported beam, point load at mid span, hand calc
check.label: simplified model, needs FEA

custom_parts.note: Strap tension, bolt shear and cradle-to-frame load path are not modelled; load = measured peak landing deceleration x tank mass.

risks.text: Per-nozzle thrust of the real hardware is unknown; the whole design scales with this swept assumption.
risks.physical_test: Static thrust-stand test of one candidate nozzle + valve at the working pressure.

risks.text: Blow-down cooling and pressure droop are not modelled: thrust and Isp fall as the tank empties and the gas cools.
risks.physical_test: Instrumented full-tank blow-down test measuring thrust vs time.
risks.tied_to: Thermal/blow-down effects not modelled; constant-Isp thrust

risks.text: Isp (70 s) is an unverified assumption and sets the propellant and tank size.
risks.physical_test: Measure Isp (thrust / mass flow) on the thrust stand.

risks.text: The landing contact load comes from a rigid-body contact model without suspension compliance (tens of g); bracket and cradle strength were checked only with hand calculations.
risks.physical_test: FEA of brackets/cradle + drop test of the suspension and mounts at the measured peak contact load.

risks.text: Aerodynamic pitching moments in flight are not simulated.
risks.physical_test: Wind-tunnel or coast-down test with a scale model / instrumented run.

risks.text: Real sensing/latency/valve response is not modelled; the controller is open-loop timing windows.
risks.physical_test: Hardware-in-the-loop test of the valve timing and IMU latency.

risks.text: Placeholder masses (nozzles, valves, regulator) are not sourced; the closed loop uses them.
risks.physical_test: Weigh candidate parts and re-run the loop with measured masses.

labels: Aerodynamics not simulated (simplified drag/momentum model only) — simplified model, needs precise validation.
Thermal effects not modeled — simplified model, needs precise validation.
Structural strength not analyzed (no FEA) — simplified model, needs precise validation.
Propulsion modeled as ideal constant-Isp thrust — simplified model, needs precise validation.
Perfect state feedback assumed; real sensing/latency not modeled — simplified model, needs precise validation.

The template's BOM says nozzle/tank mass is nominally inside the 1300 kg vehicle_mass; the closed loop conservatively adds the designed hardware ON TOP of it (upper bound on the mass effect). Nozzle count (10) is fixed by the template, so alternatives vary thrust per nozzle.
Aerodynamics not simulated; thermal/blow-down not modelled; ideal constant-Isp thrust (see verdict labels).
Closed-loop re-runs use the recorded bundle's search/Monte-Carlo budget and seed; each re-run is one seeded sample (finite-budget search noise applies).
